## Summary

Describe the change and the problem it addresses.

## Change classification

- [ ] Implementation-only
- [ ] Contract-compatible implementation
- [ ] Architecture clarification
- [ ] Architecture change
- [ ] Repository ownership change
- [ ] Dependency change
- [ ] Security-boundary change
- [ ] Compatibility-breaking change

## Architecture authority

- Owning repository:
- Repository-map entry:
- Approval-matrix status:
- Relevant ADRs:
- Relevant contracts:
- Relevant standards:
- Relevant security requirements:

## Architecture validation

- [ ] Responsibility belongs to the identified repository.
- [ ] No responsibility owned by another repository is duplicated.
- [ ] Dependencies match the documented dependency graph.
- [ ] No cyclic dependency is introduced.
- [ ] The repository approval matrix remains accurate.
- [ ] The system overview remains accurate.
- [ ] Contract compatibility has been evaluated.
- [ ] Implemented and proposed behavior are clearly distinguished.
- [ ] An ADR has been added or updated when required.

## Security and privacy

- [ ] Authorization requirements were considered.
- [ ] Scope-enforcement requirements were considered.
- [ ] Trust-boundary changes are documented.
- [ ] Secrets, personal data, live targets, and unsafe payloads are excluded.
- [ ] Security review is requested when required.

## Validation evidence

Describe tests, document checks, implementation evidence, and manual review.

## Compatibility

Describe backward compatibility, migration requirements, and affected artifacts.

## Rollback plan

Describe how the change can be reversed or state why no rollback is required.

## Affected repositories

List every repository affected directly or indirectly.
